canonical_statement: For probability measures mu and nu on compact metric spaces and a continuous real-valued cost c, the infimum of the integral of c over couplings of mu and nu equals the supremum of the integrals of real potentials phi and psi subject to phi(x) + psi(y) <= c(x,y).

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression: A new compact/continuous signed-real statement; the historical CompactMetricStatementShape is discovery input and is not accepted as exact

domain_and_universes: X : Type u, Y : Type v; compact metric Borel spaces; mu : ProbabilityMeasure X; nu : ProbabilityMeasure Y; c : X x Y -> Real
hypotheses: mu and nu are Borel probability measures
gamma ranges over probability couplings with marginals mu and nu
phi and psi are real-valued continuous potentials
conclusion: inf_gamma integral c dgamma = sup_(phi,psi feasible) (integral phi dmu + integral psi dnu)
degenerate_cases: Empty compact spaces are incompatible with an inhabited ProbabilityMeasure, but this must be checked rather than silently assumed. Constant and zero costs, Dirac marginals, singleton spaces, and absence of a feasible signed-potential representation are statement-phase mutation probes.
